newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda expects foreign inflows to rise.
newsitem.headline: Uganda expects foreign inflows to rise.

text.p: The pace of foreign investment in Uganda is likely to rise in the near-term after totalling $3.08 billion since 1991, the investment licencing agency said on Friday.

"Uganda's macro-economic environment is the best in the continent and among the best in the world in terms of facilities for promoting investment," the executive director of the Uganda Investment Authority, George Rubagumya, said in a statement marking the agency's fifth birthday.
The Authority was set up by reformist President Yoweri Museveni in 1991 to tap foreign investment. It said projects worth $1.23 billion have already started and many more were soon to be launched.
Most of the investments were in manufacturing, agriculture, construction, mining and service sectors, it said.
The projects have produced about 117,000 jobs and will create a further 13,000 in the next few months.

Uganda, trying to resuscitate its economy after two decades of dictatorships and war, has through the Authority lured foreign investors with tax holidays, promises of cheap labour and the freedom to repatriate profits.

New investors bringing in more than $5 million get a five-year tax holiday and a fully-liberalised foreign exchange market means profits can be sent home. Profits reinvested in Uganda's economy qualify for additional incentives.

To further encourage foreign investment, the government is buying private land to sell to new investors after providing water, electricity, roads and telephone services, officials in the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning said.
New investors say they are encouraged by the return of $600 million worth of properties owned by Asians and confiscated in 1972 by former dictator Idi Amin.
